note: {tool} is the toolchain's compiler, {opt} the level, {src} the absolute path of the source in its build directory, {out} the output file. Every build runs in its own directory with the build directory's real path. Variant A builds the source in directory A, variant B the same bytes in directory B, variant N the renamed source (rename.py) in directory N; the three directories have paths of equal length that differ in one character. The E4 kernels come from ../e4-energy/programs and their declared inputs and levels from ../e4-energy/matrix.json; E1's programs come from ../e1-determinism/programs.
e1_note: E1's other programs are in languages with no renamer here (C++, Go, Fortran and the rest), or need a toolchain this harness does not pick; E1's C and Rust programs use the C and Rust libraries, so they have no wasm32 build and are measured at the machine-code level only.

hashes.output-bytes: baseline: SHA-256 of the output file, the key of a cache that stores outputs by their bytes
hashes.source-key: baseline: SHA-256 of the source bytes and the build command with the build directory written as {dir}, the key of a cache keyed by source text and flags with the path remapped
hashes.machine-module: R at the machine-code level: SHA-256 of the sorted WARP-style IDs of every function of the object (machine.py)
hashes.machine-run: R at the machine-code level: the WARP-style ID of the function run (machine.py)
hashes.ir-module: R at the IR level: the alpha-equivalence hash of the linked WebAssembly module (irhash.py)
hashes.ir-run: R at the IR level: the alpha-equivalence hash of the part of the module that the export run reaches (irhash.py)

two_dir.what: the same source bytes built in directories A and B

renamed.what: the source built in A against its renamed copy built in N

opt_levels.what: the same source at two optimisation levels of one toolchain, every pair of levels

c_vs_rust.what: the C and the Rust kernel of one E4 algorithm at the same position in the list of levels

different_kernels.what: every pair of builds of two different E4 kernels, any language and level

mutations.what: each A module against itself with one opcode changed within its class, one constant changed, or one memory offset changed (irhash.mutations)
